questions.question: What is Optional<T> in Java?
options: A container that may or may not hold a value
A type of list that allows null values
An exception thrown when something is empty
explanations: Correct. Optional<T> is a container that represents the presence or absence of a value, helping to avoid NullPointerException.
It is not an access modifier.

questions.question: How do you create an Optional?
explanations: Correct. The three main factories are of() (non-null value), empty() (no value), and ofNullable() (accepts nulls).

questions.question: What does orElse() do in an Optional?
options: Returns the value of the Optional or a default value if it is empty
Throws an exception if it is empty
explanations: Correct. orElse(defaultValue) returns the value if it exists, or the default value if the Optional is empty.
It returns the actual value if it exists, not always the default.
To throw an exception you use orElseThrow().
It does not convert to null.

questions.question: What does isPresent() do in an Optional?
options: Returns true if the Optional has a value, false if it is empty
Returns the value of the Optional
Removes the value from the Optional
explanations: Correct. isPresent() returns a boolean indicating whether the Optional contains a value.
To get the value you use get() or orElse().
